model: Insurer FCFE at cost of equity on core revenue, capital retention to hold book/revenue (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 8.1% vs EPS 5yr 15.2% (>30% divergence): GAAP EPS includes equity mark-to-market (FY22 -$3.06, FY21 $18.43), so EPS CAGRs are endpoint noise. Equity 3yr 14.6% starts from the FY2022 bear-market trough. Reported revenue 3yr 24.4% is the same distortion; core revenue (premiums + NII) 10.9-11.7% is the operating anchor.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are OCF-capex less SBC ($31-46m) and describe float growth, not distributable cash -- not used. EPS 3yr CAGR undefined (FY2022 loss). Premium growth has run 8-11%/yr in a hard market; guidance for FY2026 is mid-single-digit NWP growth, two-thirds rate.

scenario_narratives.base: Commercial-lines pricing has moderated to low-single-digit renewal increases and written-premium growth has slowed to ~4%, so core revenue growth steps down from 7.5% in FY26 to mid-single digits. Underwriting holds near the long-run ~95% combined ratio (Q3-26 90.9% after Q2's 100.8%), E&S and Cincinnati Re keep growing, and the bond book reinvests at yields ~75bp above its 5.1% book yield. The ~$13bn equity portfolio earns a normal ~5% price return on top of dividends. ROE of ~11% against a 9.75% cost of equity is worth ~1.25-1.3x book, well under the price the market is paying.
scenario_narratives.bull: E&S (+8%) and Cincinnati Re (+16%, 87.6% combined) keep taking share, the commercial-lines cat problem of 2025-26 proves cyclical rather than a risk-selection failure, and the combined ratio settles at ~92-93%. Equity markets deliver ~6%/yr price appreciation on the outsized portfolio. ROE returns to the ~13% of the last decade and the market keeps paying ~1.7x book for a Dividend King compounding at 7%+.
scenario_narratives.bear: The P&C cycle softens just as cat frequency and social inflation stay elevated: commercial lines stays above 100%, California and convective-storm losses recur, and adverse development appears in long-tail umbrella/workers' comp. An equity-market correction hits the ~40% equity allocation in FY27, marking book down. ROE falls to ~9%, below the cost of equity, and the stock de-rates towards ~0.9x book -- the dividend streak survives but per-share value compounds slowly.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A P&C insurer is worth the book it compounds, not its cash flow statement. Operating cash flow is float growth and GAAP net income swings with the equity portfolio's mark-to-market, so the model values normalised earnings (underwriting + investment income + an expected, not realised, equity return) net of the equity retention needed to grow premiums with a constant book/revenue ratio, discounted at the cost of equity with debt serviced inside the flow. The result is equivalent to a terminal P/B of (ROE-g)/(CoE-g): base ~1.27x Sept-26 book on ~11% ROE against a 9.75% CoE.
key_risks_to_valuation: Equity market: $13.1bn equity securities (~0.8x book, $8.9bn unrealised gain) -- a 20% drawdown takes ~$2.1bn after tax (~$13.5/share) off book at once
Catastrophe and California wildfire exposure; commercial lines combined 104.1% in Q2-26 (92.8% in Q3-26)
Reserve adequacy in long-tail commercial casualty under social inflation
Soft-market transition compressing both premium growth and margins together
The expected equity-appreciation assumption (5% base) is the single largest judgment: each 1pp is ~1.1pp of margin and roughly $10-12/share
Discount rate: the 75bp rise in the 10y UST since September cost ~$19/share via CoE and returned ~$10/share via reinvestment yield; a reversal would roughly unwind both

inputs.share_count_basis: 153.510m shares on issue at 2026-10-22 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) + ~1.6m dilutive awards (Q3-2026 diluted weighted 155.1m) = 155.1m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. Buybacks paused in Q3-26 ($1m; 9M-26 $395m, 2.4m shares).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K XBRL: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpenseNetOfTax $37m + tax benefit $9m = $46m pre-tax (0.41% of core revenue). No separate net-share-settlement withholding line disclosed.
inputs.book_value_anchor: Shareholders' equity $16,182m at 2026-09-30 (BVPS $105.42), down from $16,671m at June: Q3 net income $459m and dividends $144m were outweighed by a $913m after-tax unrealised loss on fixed maturities as Treasury yields rose (AOCI -$951m). Equity securities at fair value $13,145m (cost $4,273m).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: the stream is after holding-company interest (~$53m/yr on $790m senior notes) so it is discounted at CoE and no debt is deducted. USD build refreshed 2026-11-19: 10y UST 5.07% (Yahoo ^TNX; was ~4.3% at the September valuation) + beta ~0.8 x 5.0% ERP = 9.07%, plus the same ~0.7pp uplift for catastrophe volatility and the equity portfolio (~0.8x book) = 9.75%. Same 9.75% in all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the scenario paths). The rate rise is matched in the flows by a reinvestment-yield uplift on the margin path (see margin_rationale).
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial for an insurer; no lease line modelled.
inputs.notes: MODEL: routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md -- insurer row (BVPS compounding x exit P/B). Implemented through the engine as FCFE at cost of equity, the same family IAG.AX used, because it is arithmetically the BVPS-compounding model (terminal P/B = (ROE-g)/(CoE-g)) and keeps the dashboard sliders live. Mapping of engine fields: revenue = CORE revenue (net earned premiums + net investment income + other; FY2025 $9,983m + $1,165m + $41m = $11,189m), i.e. reported revenue $12,631m less realized/fair-value investment gains $1,442m. 'EBITDA margin' = normalised pre-tax, pre-SBC earnings / core revenue = underwriting + investment income + an EXPECTED equity-portfolio price appreciation (base 5%/yr on ~$13.2bn = ~5.5% of revenue) in place of the reported mark-to-market gains; D&A and capex are 0; cash tax = GAAP effective rate (~19.5%, muni and dividends-received shelter; FY23-25 19.0-19.8%). 'Working capital' = required equity retention: wc_capture -140% of the revenue increase holds book/core revenue at ~1.40x (June-26 book $16,671m / FY26E core revenue ~$11.9bn), so FCFE = net income - book growth needed to write the premium. NET DEBT HELD AT ZERO: the $790m senior notes (plus $69m short-term; total_debt $859m) are serviced inside the flow, and cash is float/investment inventory, not surplus. Reported FCF ($3,092m OCF-capex) is float growth, not owner cash, and is recorded for audit only. last_fcf = FY2025 cash actually distributed (dividends $525m + buybacks $205m = $730m). Year 1 is FY2026, ~10.5 months elapsed at the valuation date with nine months reported: 9M-26 core revenue $8,926m (+7.8%; earned premiums $7,929m +7.3%, NII $962m +11.9%), operating pre-tax $1,197m (13.4% of core revenue; pre-tax $2,455m less investment gains $1,258m). Book/core revenue is now ~1.35x (Sept-26 book $16,182m / FY26E core ~$12.0bn); the -140% retention is left unchanged because the dip is a rate-driven bond mark that pulls to par, not a change in required capital. Operating pre-tax (pre-tax less investment gains): FY21 $1,289m (17.9% of core rev), FY22 $773m (9.6%), FY23 $1,149m (12.9%), FY24 $1,467m (14.7%), FY25 $1,538m (13.7%, LA wildfires). UPDATE 2026-11-19 (Q3-2026 10-Q): same model as the 2026-09-26 valuation. Changed: FY26 growth and margin (nine-month actuals), FY27 growth (written-premium slowdown), a reinvestment-yield uplift on the FY27+ margin path and the cost of equity (both from the ~75bp rise in the 10y UST). Deliberately unchanged: FY28+ growth paths, normalised ~95% base combined ratio, 5%/6%/3% expected equity appreciation, tax 19.5%, SBC 0.41%, wc_capture -140%, terminal growth, scenario weights. These would move on: a second year of commercial combined ratio >100% or adverse reserve development (margins), a change in the equity allocation (appreciation), a statutory tax change, or sustained buybacks shrinking book/revenue (retention).

bear.margin_rationale: Soft market plus persistent cat/social-inflation drag: combined ratio ~98-99% -> operating ~10.5%; equity appreciation only 3%/yr (~3.3% of revenue); FY27 carries an equity-market drawdown; same reinvestment-yield uplift as base. FY26 17.5%: nine months are banked, with a heavy-cat Q4 and a weak equity quarter. ROE ~9%, below the 9.75% CoE, so book trades below 1x.
bear.growth_rationale: FY26 +7.2% (nine months reported limit the downside); FY27 onward unchanged.

base.margin_rationale: FY26: nine-month operating pre-tax 13.4% of core revenue plus a normal Q4 (~$500m) gives ~14.1% for the year, plus 5% expected price appreciation on the ~$13.1bn equity book (~5.5% of revenue) plus SBC add-back 0.4pp = 20.0%. Thereafter the normalised 13.5% operating margin (FY21-25 average 13.8%, ~95% combined ratio) + ~5.3% equity appreciation + 0.4pp, with a reinvestment-yield uplift building from +0.2pp (FY27) to +1.0pp (FY32 onward): ~$19bn of fixed maturities at a 5.11% book yield rolls into a market ~75bp higher. Implies ROE ~11% on book.
base.growth_rationale: FY26 +7.5% from 9M-26 core revenue +7.8% and a slower Q4. FY27 cut 5.5% -> 4.5%: 9M-26 net written premiums grew only ~4% (earned + unearned change), Q3 agency renewal premiums +1%, standard commercial renewal pricing down to low-single digits; NII still growing ~10%. FY28 onward unchanged, decelerating to nominal-GDP 3%.

bull.margin_rationale: Combined ratio ~92-93% (E&S and Cincinnati Re mix shift, California repricing done) -> operating ~16%, plus 6% equity appreciation (~6.3% of revenue), plus the same reinvestment-yield uplift as base (+0.2pp FY27 to +1.0pp FY32+). FY26 20.5% assumes a benign Q4 like Q3's 90.9% combined ratio. ROE ~13%, in line with the 2016-2025 record.
bull.growth_rationale: FY26 +7.8% (9M +7.8%); FY27 trimmed 7.0% -> 6.0% on the written-premium slowdown; later years unchanged.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged at 20/50/30. Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the pricing cycle is turning (renewal premiums +1% in Q3-26), Q2-26 commercial combined ratio was 104%, and book is levered ~0.8x to equity markets near highs. Base 50%. Bull 30% (below 35%): it needs benign cats, sustained E&S/Re growth AND a continued equity bull market at once, though CINF's 65-year dividend record and conservative reserving make it a credible path rather than a stretch.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
